description: A reified 'follows' relation: a study that follows a protocol (subject = study, object = protocol) — the method hop of the provenance spine, claim ← supports ← evidence ← grounds ← study --follows--> protocol. The subject MUST be a study (tech.scios.rrgi.study) and the object MUST be a protocol (tech.scios.rrgi.protocol). Adopted from the MIRA community schema (github.com/MIRA-science/schema, mira.yaml: slot follows, domain Study, range Protocol). MIRA's slot is MULTIVALUED, so one edge record per study-protocol pair — a study following two protocols carries two follows edges. An AT Protocol lexicon cannot type strongRef endpoints, so this rule is normative prose here; enforcement lives in the AppView indexer and in every write path. RRGI's intentional divergence (matching every RRGI relation): subject/object are dual-addressed via com.atproto.repo.strongRef (uri + cid, CID mandatory) instead of a bare reference, so the edge pins exact content versions and cannot rot — an extension intended to be proposed upstream to MIRA. No upstream atproto lexicon exists for this relation; authored here from the MIRA schema.

subject.description: Dual-addressed reference (URI + CID) to the following node (the study). MUST be a study (tech.scios.rrgi.study); the lexicon cannot type a strongRef endpoint, so the indexer enforces this. CID mandatory.

object.description: Dual-addressed reference (URI + CID) to the followed node (the protocol). MUST be a protocol (tech.scios.rrgi.protocol); one edge record per study-protocol pair (MIRA's follows is multivalued). CID mandatory.

description.description: Optional elaboration: how the study follows or adapts this protocol.
